To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human brain tracks the spatiotemporal dynamics of real-world object size and animacy, and that these processes are mediated by the ventral occipitotemporal cortex (VOTC) and the temporoparietal junction (TPJ), respectively.
the brain processes real-world size and animacy in different ways and that the neural mechanisms underlying the processing of size and animacy differ in terms of their spatiotemporal dynamics.

animacy and size are processed in the brain as two independent dimensions, but that their neural dynamics are highly interrelated, and that the brain uses these two dimensions to create an integrated perception of objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of the perception of size and animacy of real-world objects, and how these properties are processed in the human brain.
the spatiotemporal processing of real-world size and animacy in the human brain.
how the human brain represents and processes the properties of size and animacy of real-world objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is a complex system of neurons and neural networks.
the brain is a very complex and sophisticated organ, and the human brain is the most complex of all.
the neural mechanisms of animacy and size are not only different but also interact with each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
animacy and size are two fundamental features of objects that can be processed by the human brain in a very fast, efficient and parallel way.
animacy is a basic property of the visual world, that is represented by the human brain and that is processed in a spatiotemporal manner.
the neural mechanisms underlying real-world object size and animacy are distinct from those of physical object size and animate/ inanimate object categories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human brain uses a shared network of regions for processing both animacy and size, which we term a “perceptual hierarchy”.
the human visual system is able to rapidly and automatically integrate object size and animacy information to form a coherent representation of the visual world.
the human brain uses the same neural resources to represent object size and animacy.
